title: paperfind
description: Today's arXiv, read for you by an AI agent. Describe your research (or pick a sample researcher) and the agent screens every new paper in your fields: titles first, then abstracts, with a score and a one-line reason each. Tell the assistant what's off and it finds the cause in your interest profile, edits a draft, and re-scores real papers under the draft before you accept the change. The Agent log shows every model request and tool call. Simplifications: arXiv only; the feed covers papers announced during your visit (the RSS feed, or the search API on weekends); one model, the one you select, does all screening and the assistant; nothing is kept after the visit ends.
instructions: Pick a sample researcher, or describe your research and paste a few paper titles or arXiv links. The first papers appear in about 15 seconds; the rest fill in as they're scored. Then click "Not for me…" on a paper, or tell the assistant what's wrong, and apply its tested proposal. Open the Agent log to watch each model request and tool call.

inference.estimateBasis: Measured with Claude Haiku 5.5 at list prices through a local stand-in for the gateway: screening ~440 papers cost $0.017 (11 requests), one assistant message $0.004 (5 requests), re-screening after a change $0.014. A visit with several changes stays under about $0.25. Other models are priced differently; portal limits apply.
